beats.say: The coding round wants code you could ship.
Not clever code. Clean code, with the right speed, that handles failure.
beats.label: What they score
beats.head: Clean, fast enough, safe

beats.say: Three habits: pick the right structure, stream big data, and write for production.
beats.label: Track 4 · Python and data coding

check.prompt: You must check if an id is in a collection of ten million ids. Which structure?
check.why: A set uses a hash, so the check takes one step. A list reads every item.

beats.say: First: pick the right data structure.
To check if a value is in a list, Python reads the whole list.
beats.label: A list
beats.head: Search in a list: slow

beats.say: A set or a dict uses a hash. The same check takes one step.
beats.label: A set or a dict
beats.head: Search in a set: one step

beats.say: Use a dict to count. A deque for a queue. And a heap for the top few items.
beats.label: Reach for these

beats.say: Second: the file is bigger than memory.
Do not load it all. A generator gives you one row at a time.
beats.label: Generators
beats.head: One row at a time

beats.say: Memory stays flat, even for a file of 100 gigabytes.
beats.label: The result
beats.head: Constant memory

check.prompt: What does idempotent mean for a task?
options: Run it twice, and the result is the same
check.why: An idempotent task is safe to retry: a second run does not change the result.

beats.say: Third: write it like production code.
A network call can fail. So retry, and wait longer after each try.
beats.label: Retries
beats.head: Retry with backoff

beats.say: And make the task idempotent. Run it twice, and the result is the same.
beats.label: Idempotent
beats.head: Run twice, same result

beats.say: Then add one small test. It shows the interviewer you check your own work.
beats.label: Tests
beats.head: One small test

beats.say: Last: how do you make Python faster?
For waiting on a network or a disk, use threads or asyncio.
beats.label: Waiting work
beats.head: Waiting: threads or asyncio

beats.say: For heavy maths on the CPU, use processes. The interpreter lock blocks threads there.
beats.label: CPU work
beats.head: CPU: processes

beats.say: Quick recap of Python for data coding.
Hash for lookups. Generators for big files. And retries with idempotent tasks.
beats.label: Python and data coding

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
